newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P cuts Peugeot units outlook, confirms debt.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Peugeot units outlook, confirms debt.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it downgraded the outlook for units of Peugeot SA, part of the PSA Peugeot Citroen group, to negative from stable.
It confirmed its A minus long-term and A-2 short-term ratings on the debt, it said in a statement.
The S&P confirmation and outlook downgrade affects the whole PSA Peugeot Citroen group, an S&P official later said.
The revision in outlook reflects uncertainties over PSA's ability "to sustain its competitive position and its profitability in the current Europe environment," S&P said in a statement.
The move also took into account a general deterioration in European market conditions and PSA's lack of significant growth opportunities outside Europe, it added.
The ratings reflect PSA's position as the third largest carmaker in the increasingly competitive European automotive industry and its conservative financial profile, it said.
The group's dependence on the French market, with 37 percent of group sales in 1996, accounted for the significant fall in its operating margin.

The home market is confronted by intensification of a price war and the end of the state rebate system. PSA's ability to sustain a satisfactory level of profitability, in the face of declining volumes and sales discounts, "remains to be seen".
It has a modest presence in markets outside western Europe, which account for only 13 percent of group sales.
